accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding INSAT-1 series:
1. The first INSAT satellites were bought abroad.
2. The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983.
3. The series began from 1992 with INSAT-2A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The INSAT-1 satellites were procured from abroad and the INSAT system was commissioned in 1983. Statement 3 is false because the INSAT-2 series began in 1992.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the series start dates before considering the combined code.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: KALPANA-1, originally known as METSAT, was primarily designed as a/an
accepted.x: KALPANA-1, earlier called METSAT, was an exclusive meteorological satellite and was launched by PSLV in September 2002.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite’s distinctive name with its specialised purpose.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: GSAT-8 — Cyclone-warning satellite without communication payloads
accepted.x: EDUSAT, also designated GSAT-3, was intended for education and provided two-way classroom links. The other satellites have been matched with incorrect functions.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure purpose-satellite pair and reject swapped applications.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: EDUSAT (GSAT-3) was launched on 20 September 2004 by
o: LVM3-M5 from Sriharikota into a sub-GTO
Ariane-5 from Kourou into a geostationary transfer orbit
accepted.x: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01, had a mass of 1,950.5 kg and was positioned at 74°E.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, launcher and orbital-position clues rather than relying on the satellite’s name alone.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations regarding INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR is correct?
o: INSAT-3D—1983; television broadcasting; INSAT-3DR—1992; mobile communication
INSAT-3D—2013; advanced meteorology; INSAT-3DR—2016; advanced meteorology
accepted.x: INSAT-3D was launched in 2013 and INSAT-3DR in 2016; both serve advanced meteorological purposes.
accepted.tq: Compare the two closely named satellites by year and common application.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: The principal purpose of INSAT-3D includes advanced monitoring of
accepted.x: INSAT-3D provides advanced meteorological observations relating to cyclones, monsoon and rainfall.
accepted.tq: Identify the application cluster that belongs to meteorological satellites.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-8 is correct?
o: It was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload.
It was launched in 2020 by GSLV-F01 for two-way classroom links.
It was launched in 2018 by Falcon 9 and carried only a military payload.
It was launched in 2004 by PSLV and functioned as an exclusive weather satellite.
accepted.x: GSAT-8 was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload; GSAT-10 and GSAT-15 also carried GAGAN payloads.
accepted.tq: Use the date-launcher-payload combination to distinguish GSAT-8 from nearby GSAT missions.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding GSAT-11 is correct?
o: It is an experimental satellite launched in 1981 for communication testing.
It is a navigation satellite carrying only search-and-rescue transponders.
It is an approximately 5.8-tonne ISRO-built communication satellite intended to support high-speed internet and rural broadband.
It is a meteorological satellite exclusively used for cyclone warnings.
accepted.x: GSAT-11 is the heaviest ISRO-built communication satellite, weighing approximately 5.8 tonnes, and supports high-speed internet, rural broadband and Digital India.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive largest/heaviest description and application pair.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of their stated launch dates:
A. GSAT-30
B. KALPANA-1
C. EDUSAT
D. GSAT-8
accepted.x: KALPANA-1 was launched in 2002, EDUSAT in 2004, GSAT-8 in 2011 and GSAT-30 in 2020.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the middle satellites by year.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: GSAT-N2, also designated GSAT-20, is associated primarily with
accepted.x: GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20), listed with a November 2024 launch, is intended for broadband and in-flight connectivity.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the newer GSAT designation from similarly numbered communication satellites.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: CMS-03, also referred to as GSAT-7R, is intended primarily for the
accepted.x: CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Navy satellite, listed as a November 2025 LVM3-M5 launch with a mass of about 4,410 kg.
accepted.tq: Use the service-specific role to separate CMS-03 from GSAT-7A and GSAT-7B.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7, known as Rukmini, serves the Navy.
2. GSAT-7A, known as Angry Bird, serves the Indian Air Force.
3. GSAT-7B was proposed for the Army.
4. GSAT-6 has a large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. GSAT-7, GSAT-7A and proposed GSAT-7B are associated respectively with the Navy, Air Force and Army, while GSAT-6 has a large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic applications.
accepted.tq: Check each service assignment independently before selecting the comprehensive code.
accepted.sec: INSAT/GSAT series → purpose + launch date

accepted.s: In the Disaster Warning System, cyclone warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai are
o: sent upward through S-band and received through C-band by all receivers without selection
sent upward through UHF and received through MF by television households
sent upward through C-band and received through S-band by selectively addressable receivers
sent upward through Ku-band and received through Ka-band only by military stations
accepted.x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.
accepted.tq: Trace the communication path in order: uplink band, downlink band and receiver type.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication for disaster management - APSDMA, satellite phones

accepted.s: Which organisation receives Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data supplied by SDSC-SHAR for disaster-management purposes?
accepted.x: SDSC-SHAR supplies Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA).
accepted.tq: Identify the receiving disaster-management authority rather than the supplying centre.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication for disaster management - APSDMA, satellite phones

accepted.s: INSAT’s search-and-rescue transponders operate under the international programme known as
accepted.x: INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international COSPAS-SARSAT programme.
accepted.tq: Separate search-and-rescue terminology from navigation and education programmes.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication for disaster management - APSDMA, satellite phones

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about a geostationary satellite is NOT correct?
o: Its orbital plane is the equatorial plane with zero inclination.
Its orbital period is approximately 24 hours.
It orbits at approximately 35,786 km above the equator.
Its fixed orbital height varies according to the mass of the satellite.
accepted.x: The geostationary orbital height is fixed and does not depend on the satellite’s mass. The other statements correctly describe geostationary orbit.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by checking the physical condition that does not affect orbital height.
accepted.sec: Geostationary orbit - altitude, period, direction, plane, GTO

accepted.s: A geostationary satellite appears stationary to an observer because it
o: moves from east to west in a polar plane
moves from west to east in the equatorial plane with a period matching Earth’s rotation
remains permanently fixed above the North Pole
moves randomly around the Earth at a very low altitude
accepted.x: A geostationary satellite moves west to east in the equatorial plane and has a 24-hour period, matching Earth’s rotation.
accepted.tq: Combine direction, plane and period to explain the apparent stationary position.
accepted.sec: Geostationary orbit - altitude, period, direction, plane, GTO

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the usual process of placing a communication satellite in geostationary orbit?
o: The launcher places it in an elliptical GTO, after which the satellite’s own motor raises it to GEO.
The satellite first descends into the atmosphere and is then lifted by solar radiation.
The launcher directly places it in a circular polar orbit and the satellite remains there.
The launcher places it directly in a sub-GTO and no onboard propulsion is required.
accepted.x: Launch vehicles generally inject satellites into an elliptical geostationary transfer orbit (GTO); the satellite’s own motor raises it to geostationary orbit (GEO).
accepted.tq: Distinguish the transfer orbit from the final geostationary orbit.
accepted.sec: Geostationary orbit - altitude, period, direction, plane, GTO

accepted.s: EOS-05, as listed for September 2026, was placed in a
accepted.x: EOS-05 was placed in a sub-geostationary transfer orbit, or sub-GTO, in September 2026.
accepted.tq: Recognise the precise transfer-orbit term instead of substituting GEO or LEO.
accepted.sec: Geostationary orbit - altitude, period, direction, plane, GTO

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane?
accepted.x: INSAT-3A, INSAT-4A, INSAT-4B and GSAT-8 are among the Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane.
accepted.tq: Group the satellites by launcher and location, rejecting satellites associated with Indian or US launchers.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: INSAT-1B was launched on the US Space Shuttle. APPLE flew on Ariane, GSAT-N2 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral, and GSAT-30 from Kourou.
accepted.tq: Use the launcher-location pair as the decisive clue in a foreign-launch question.
accepted.sec: Foreign launches of Indian communication satellites

accepted.s: GSAT-N2 was launched by
o: US Space Shuttle from Kennedy Space Center
accepted.x: GSAT-N2 was launched by SpaceX’s Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral.
accepted.tq: Separate the recent commercial foreign launch from the earlier Ariane launches.
accepted.sec: Foreign launches of Indian communication satellites

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains APPLE?
o: Asian Public Platform for Long-distance Education, launched in 2004 as EDUSAT
Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment, launched in 1981 as India’s first experimental communication satellite
Aerial Payload and Propulsion Laboratory Experiment, launched in 2002 as a navigation satellite
Advanced Polar Payload Launch Experiment, launched in 1992 as India’s first meteorological satellite
accepted.x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment and was India’s first experimental communication satellite, launched in 1981.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with its historical role.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: Which of the following is a feature of the multipurpose INSAT design?
o: Telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue are integrated on one geostationary platform.
Only military communication is provided through a network of polar satellites.
Only weather imaging is performed, without broadcasting or disaster services.
Education and telemedicine are excluded from the satellite-based service framework.
accepted.x: INSAT integrates telecommunications, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue on one geostationary platform. It is regarded as one of the largest domestic systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
accepted.tq: Select the option that captures the full multipurpose design rather than a single service.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: The INSAT system is a joint venture involving which of the following groups of organisations?
o: DoS, DoT, IMD, All India Radio and Doordarshan
DRDO, RBI, SEBI, NITI Aayog and Election Commission
ISRO, WHO, UNESCO, IMF and World Bank
Ministry of Defence, Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard only
accepted.x: The INSAT system is a joint venture of the Department of Space, Department of Telecommunications, India Meteorological Department, All India Radio and Doordarshan.
accepted.tq: Check institutional composition carefully; the trap is substitution of unrelated national bodies.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the management of the INSAT system is correct?
o: The system is coordinated by Doordarshan alone and controlled from Sriharikota.
The system is coordinated by the INSAT Coordination Committee and controlled from the Master Control Facility at Hassan.
The system is coordinated by the Cyclone Warning Centre and controlled from Kourou.
The system is coordinated by NSIL alone and controlled from Cape Canaveral.
accepted.x: The INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC) coordinates the system, while control is exercised from the Master Control Facility at Hassan in Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the coordinating body from the operational control facility.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: INSAT-4C was lost because
o: GSLV-F01 failed during the EDUSAT mission
Falcon 9 failed during the GSAT-N2 mission
accepted.x: INSAT-4C was lost in 2006 when GSLV-F02 failed. It was replaced by INSAT-4CR, launched in September 2007 by GSLV-F04.
accepted.tq: Link the failed satellite with the correct launch vehicle and year.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the present operational arrangement described for India’s communication satellites?
o: Ten in-orbit communication satellites were transferred to NSIL in 2022, and NSIL operates 11 communication satellites with about 300 transponders through more than 150 agreements.
NSIL operates only three satellites with fewer than 30 transponders and no service agreements.
The INSAT Coordination Committee transferred every communication satellite to the Indian Navy in 2022.
All communication satellites remain under Doordarshan, which operates exactly 19 transponders through 10 agreements.
accepted.x: Ten in-orbit communication satellites were transferred to NSIL in 2022; NSIL operates 11 communication satellites with approximately 300 transponders through more than 150 agreements.
accepted.tq: Track the institutional transfer and retain the associated counts rather than focusing on only one figure.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - APPLE, first INSAT, design, failures, heaviest, operator

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the C and extended-C bands is correct?
o: They are used only for mobile satellite services and DWS downlink.
They are typically used for telecommunications and television distribution in the 4–8 GHz range.
They are used mainly for DTH and VSAT in the 12–18 GHz range.
They are used exclusively for high-throughput broadband in the 26–40 GHz range.
accepted.x: C and extended-C bands are typically used for telecommunications and television distribution and operate in the 4–8 GHz range.
accepted.tq: Match each frequency range with its characteristic service before eliminating the swapped bands.
accepted.sec: Transponder bands - C, extended C, Ku, Ka, S; bands not used; HTS

accepted.s: Ku-band transponders are commonly associated with
o: DWS downlink and mobile satellite services only in the S-band range
military services only in the UHF range
high-throughput broadband only in the Ka-band range
DTH and VSAT services in the 12–18 GHz range
accepted.x: Ku-band operates typically in the 12–18 GHz range and is used for Direct-to-Home (DTH) and VSAT services.
accepted.tq: Use the service-frequency pair to distinguish Ku from C, Ka and S bands.
accepted.sec: Transponder bands - C, extended C, Ku, Ka, S; bands not used; HTS

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: S-band — television distribution in the 4–8 GHz range
C-band — DTH in the 12–18 GHz range
UHF — education channels through Swayam Prabha
accepted.x: Ka-band is used for high-throughput broadband, including applications associated with GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2. S-band is associated with mobile satellite services and DWS downlink, while UHF has military applications.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive high-throughput broadband pair and identify the band swap in the distractors.
accepted.sec: Transponder bands - C, extended C, Ku, Ka, S; bands not used; HTS

accepted.s: Which of the following satellites is associated with UHF, S and C bands in the stated communication configuration?
accepted.x: CMS-03 has UHF, S and C bands in the stated configuration; UHF is associated with military applications.
accepted.tq: Identify the satellite from the unusual combination of three transponder bands.
accepted.sec: Transponder bands - C, extended C, Ku, Ka, S; bands not used; HTS

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only high-throughput or broadband satellites?
accepted.x: GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.
accepted.tq: Group satellites by service category and reject meteorological, educational and strategic-only sets.
accepted.sec: Transponder bands - C, extended C, Ku, Ka, S; bands not used; HTS

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an application served by the INSAT/GSAT system?
o: Extraction of petroleum directly from underground reservoirs
accepted.x: INSAT/GSAT applications include DSNG, mobile satellite services and satellite-aided search and rescue, but satellites do not directly extract petroleum from underground reservoirs.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated activity among the recognised communication and service applications.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Swayam Prabha is correct?
o: It uses INSAT-4CR to provide satellite-aided search-and-rescue services.
It uses KALPANA-1 to transmit cyclone warnings to coastal receivers.
It uses GSAT-11 to provide only military broadband channels.
It uses GSAT-15 to beam 40 free DTH education channels.
accepted.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free Direct-to-Home education channels.
accepted.tq: Match the named education initiative with its satellite and channel count.

accepted.s: The ISRO Telemedicine Network is intended to link
o: cyclone warning centres and foreign launch sites exclusively
only geostationary satellites and launch vehicles
urban television studios and commercial cinemas
accepted.x: The ISRO Telemedicine Network links border posts and rural clinics through satellite-enabled medical services.
accepted.tq: Identify the beneficiary locations that reveal the network’s telemedicine purpose.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with an INSAT/GSAT service?
o: GRAMSAT — rural development and village-oriented communication support
EDUSAT — military-only communication for the Navy
DTH — launch vehicle guidance from GTO
accepted.x: GRAMSAT is associated with rural and village-oriented communication support. EDUSAT serves education, while DSNG and DTH are communication applications rather than orbital functions.
